cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing a letter to the believers in Colossae (Colossians 1:1-2). He just told them they've been made complete in Christ, and that God canceled the debt against them by nailing it to the cross (Colossians 2:10, 14). Now he turns to what they eat and drink, and to anybody who'd size them up over it, like the coworker who peeks at your plate and goes, “Oh. You're eating THAT?”

cards.question: So Paul tells the Colossians: let no one ___ you by what you eat or drink.
True or false: Paul tells the Colossians not to let anyone judge them with regard to a Sabbath.

cards.text: Then Paul calls food, drink, feasts, New Moons and Sabbaths a shadow of the things to come. It's like the smell drifting out of my oven, friend: it tells you the real cookies are coming, but I have NEVER boxed up a smell.

cards.question: Paul calls food, drink, feasts, New Moons and Sabbaths a shadow of the things to come. Who does the body that casts that shadow belong to?

cards.text: Next, Paul warns about someone who delights in false humility and the worship of angels, and who leans on speculation about what he has seen. That's me swearing I once saw a cookie as big as my oven, and you asking for a picture, and me suddenly getting VERY busy.

cards.question: Paul warns about someone who delights in false humility and the worship of angels. He tells the Colossians not to let that person ___ them with speculation about what he has seen.
True or false: Paul says the person who delights in false humility is puffed up by a very spiritual mind.

cards.text: Then Paul shows what's gone wrong with this guy, using a picture of a body. It's like my mixer with its plug yanked out of the wall, friend: looks GREAT on the counter, mixes NOTHING.

cards.question: Paul says the person who delights in false humility has lost connection to the ___.

cards.text: From the head, the whole body is supported and knit together by its joints and ligaments. Like dough mixed just right, friend: every bit holding on to every other bit.

cards.question: In Paul's picture of a body knit together from the head, who causes the body to grow?

cards.text: Then Paul asks the Colossians a question. If you have died with Christ to the spiritual forces of the world, why live as though you still belonged to the world?

cards.question: Paul asks the Colossians why, if they died with Christ to the spiritual forces of the world, they still submit to the world's ___.

cards.text: Here's how those rules sound: “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch!” Friend, I have met smoke alarms with more chill than that.

cards.question: Right after quoting “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch!” Paul says these will all do something with use. What?
Paul quotes the world's regulations, “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch!” and says these will all perish with use. What does he say they are based on?

cards.text: Paul says these restrictions indeed have an appearance of wisdom, with their self-prescribed worship, their false humility and their harsh treatment of the body. Looks wise, SOUNDS wise, got a whole wise outfit on.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says restrictions with self-prescribed worship, false humility and harsh treatment of the body are of real value against the indulgence of the flesh.
